small_guidance:
- The conv (nn.Conv2d on 64×64×128×128 with k=3) almost certainly dominates this 6.18 ms vs the 3.43 ms baseline; further tuning of the BN/Mish epilogue won't close the gap. If staying small, at least drop the two-pass eval-mode (`_mish_bn_kernel`) tile sweep to include a `BLOCK=16384, num_warps=8` config and use `channels_last` so the per-channel scale/shift gather becomes a contiguous broadcast.
- In training mode, fuse the final apply-BN pass with the Mish so the stats kernel writes y, and a single second pass reads x (not y) and recomputes Mish + applies BN — eliminates the intermediate `y` tensor write/read (~64 MB).
- Replace the `(offs // HW) % C` channel computation with an explicit 2D grid `(N, ceil(C*HW/BLOCK))` and pass channel via program_id to remove the integer divide in the inner loop.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)`, K-dim = `IC*KH*KW = 576`, M=OC=128, output spatial = 126*126. Start with safe tiles `(BM,BN,BK)=(64,64,32) num_warps=4 num_stages=2` in an autotune list including `(32,64,16)` and `(64,32,16)`. Fuse the Mish (`x*tanh(softplus(x))`) into the GEMM epilogue on the accumulator before the store.
- At eval time, fold BatchNorm's affine (`scale = gamma/sqrt(var+eps)`, `shift = beta - mean*scale`) into the conv epilogue as well — multiply the accumulator by per-OC scale and add shift right after the Mish, eliminating the second kernel entirely. At training time keep a separate stats pass over the conv+Mish output, then a fused BN-apply kernel.
- Use `channels_last` (NHWC) memory layout end-to-end so the GEMM-K reduction (over IC*KH*KW) has IC contiguous, and the per-channel scale/shift broadcast is a contiguous vector load along the BN axis.
